newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold down on sluggish buys, subdued trends.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold down on sluggish buys, subdued trends.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed 25 rupees lower at 4,770 rupees per 10 grammes down against previous closing of 4,795 rupees on the back of sluggish seasonal buying while trends in the world markets were subdued.
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 200 rupees lower at 55,800 rupees per piece against the previous close of 56,000 rupees. They were down by 200 rupees each on Saturday.

** Silver (.999) closed 70 rupees lower at 7,355 rupees per kg against the previous close of 7,425 rupees amid fresh arrivals of imported silver while industrial buyers kept to the sidelines. Silver was down by 25 rupees per kg on Saturday.

Gold 24 carat closed 25 rupees lower at 4,770 rupees per 10 grammes down against the previous close of 4,795 rupees on the back of sluggish seasonal buying while subdued trends in the world market prompted fresh offerings, dealers said.
Gold was down by 10 rupees per 10 gramme on Saturday.
Prices of gold biscuits (116.50 gramme) closed 200 rupees lower at 55,800 rupees each.

Silver (.999) closed 70 rupees lower at 7,355 rupees per kg down against the previous close of 7,425 rupees amid fresh arrivals of the imported silver while industrial buyers kept sidelines expecting further price erosion. Silver was down by 25 rupees per kg on Saturday.

"Market sentiments for both the precious metals remained weak at the close of the session amid expectation that state government in Maharashtra may reduce sales tax on bullion to half percent from 2 percent," said M. L. Damani, president of the Bombay Bullion Exchange.

"We have represented for the same to the finance minister of Maharashtra and I am expecting affirmative announcement by minister while presenting state budget on Tuesday," he added. (Conversion $1=35.87 rupees)
